Hi Sophie / Miguel —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick written recap so we have a shared baseline and clear next steps. Please correct anything I’ve mis-captured.

Summary of current state (what you told us)
- Heavy reliance on external completion APIs: OpenAI for chat + Anthropic for assistant flows; roughly $40–60k/month in API spend across completions + embeddings.
- Two pain patterns: (1) cost volatility during peak batches (billing spikes tied to long-context chats), (2) intermittent rate-limit impacts on synchronous features (search & chat).
- Data residency note: PHI-adjacent logs need to remain in US-only regions; you also have compliance gating for SOC 2 evidence and audit logs.
- Tech stack: primary backend on AWS (EKS), event bus on Kafka, realtime inference orchestrated via a microservice that calls vendor APIs. Embeddings are stored in an internal vector DB (Pinecone today).

Success criteria for any migration / off-ramp
1) Equivalent or improved response quality for top 12 intents (we’ll validate with your test prompts).
2) End-to-end 95th percentile latency within ~1.2x of current (SLA target: 600ms p95 for chat simple flows).
3) Meaningful unit-cost reduction target: initial goal ~30–60% token cost savings vs current blended vendor pricing.
4) Full compatibility with function-calling/webhook style integrations and streaming for long-response flows.
5) Auditability: request/response logs and KV-prefetch traces retained to meet your compliance audits.

Compatibility & model requirements
- Must support streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings, and token counting consistent with your billing.
- Reasonable parity on safety / content filters; you use Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows today.
- Ability to run in a dedicated VPC or Dedicated Redwood pool for isolation.

Initial model shortlist we discussed (candidate families to test in pilot)
- Llama-3 13B (int8 quant) — strong instruction-following; cost-efficient on T4/RTX-class GPUs.
- Mistral-Instruct 7B (8-bit) — compact, good for assistant style prompts and lower latency.
- Redwood-3-small-quant (Redwood curated) — engineered for streaming and continuous KV cache efficiency.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) Redwood to send a one-pager pilot plan + model shortlist perf expectations (what we’ll measure). Attached: redwood_model_shortlist.pdf.
2) HealthOps to share: (a) 12 canonical prompts for acceptance tests, (b) a small set of anonymized request logs (<= 50k tokens) for perf/cost estimation, and (c) procurement contact for SOW.
3) We’ll provision an isolated pilot environment (Dedicated pool or VPC) and run a 2-week smoke + 2-week evaluation with reporting on latency, cost, and fidelity.
4) Target: Pilot kickoff week of Aug 10 — Myers / HealthOps procurement to confirm SOW and timeline.

Attachments referenced: redwood_model_shortlist.pdf, soc2_summary.pdf, healthops_migration_checklist.xlsx
